text:
Nashville has won the last eight games Reid Schaefer has dressed for, and he has been along for the ride more than driving it. The 6-foot-5 winger, a first-round pick of his hometown Oilers who came to the Predators in the 2023 Mattias Ekholm trade, plays about 10 and a half minutes a night in a bottom-six role built on contact: 26 hits in 13 games.

The scoring is thin, one goal and one assist, and he is shooting 8.3% on 12 shots. That part looks more like bad luck than a real problem, since his chances (0.87 expected goals, our measure of shot quality) roughly match the one goal. The bigger issue is territory. Nashville has taken 43% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, a bit worse than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had the same pattern last season: around replacement level, with the team creating little offense when he played. Forwards drafted around his slot since 2005 scored a median 0.33 points a game in their first full season; he is at 0.15 through 13 games, a small sample.
headline: Reid Schaefer rides along on Nashville's winning run
